note: An attachment compressed with a method that is neither stored nor deflate. Section 7's remedy is proportionate rather than uniform: if the ROOT DOCUMENT used such a method the archive is refused, because there is no document to return, but if an attachment did, the reader drops that attachment, records a diagnostic and returns the document. Refusing a whole library because one photograph used an unusual method would be disproportionate. Nothing in the corpus reached that remedy before this file. THE DROPPED ENTRY'S NAME CONTAINS A SLASH, and that is load-bearing rather than realistic. Section 6.3 puts a container diagnostic in the `#/entries/` pointer space, because an archive entry is not part of the document and no pointer into the document can locate one - and there the member name is one RFC 6901 reference token, so a `/` inside it MUST be escaped as `~1`. An attachment name is the one place in this format where a member name routinely contains a slash, so a reader that forgets to escape emits `#/entries/attachments/photo.jpg`, which no runner will match, while every attachment name without a slash passes either way. Renaming this entry to something without a directory removes that coverage and nothing goes red. `notes/readable.txt` is kept and listed, so the drop is provably scoped rather than total: a reader that dropped every attachment on meeting one bad method would otherwise pass. The body of the dropped entry is not valid bzip2 data and never could be read as any, deliberately - a conforming reader refuses it on the METHOD, before attempting to decompress. A reader that inflated first would fail on the body and could report the wrong cause, and this file cannot tell those two apart, which is a limitation rather than a defect. Method 12 is legal in APPNOTE and simply not available in every target language, which is what section 7 is about; the case would work the same with any method outside stored and deflate. This archive is hand-built, because archive/zip refuses to write a method it has no compressor for - which is every method but the two section 7 allows.
